## Settled positions on these variables

- **POSTNA-3** · vars: ENEMY.engagement_control, ENEMY.regeneration, SANCT.laos, SANCT.cambodia · While the enemy controls whether to accept battle and regenerates in sanctuary, attrition has no crossover point; a strategy that waits for one waits for something the geometry does not permit (TNA G-8)
- **POSTNA-4** · vars: TRAIL.capacity, TRAIL.tonnage_arriving · On the opening date the enemy's external requirement from the North is of the order of 20 tons a day against a Trail of 20–30 tons a day and an uncounted sea route; Trail capacity is elastic with labour, so interdiction is judged only by tonnage arriving below the requirement, never by trucks or porters destroyed (TNA G-9)
- **POS003-1** · vars: FIND.main_force, FIX.capability, STRIKE.responsiveness · Airborne radar and signals reconnaissance find the enemy's movement in the open and his headquarters' transmitters, never his regiments under canopy; their value in any engagement equals what can be put on a track within the hour, and an improvement in finding is never claimed as an improvement in fixing (003 §2 F003-5; §4.P2–P5)
- **POS003-2** · vars: INFIL.sea, SANCT.cambodia, TRAIL.tonnage_arriving · In this war the sea route to the South's coast closed in 1964 under observation and the enemy's southern supply moved to Sihanoukville from June 1965; supply through Cambodia, not by sea, is the principal external line into III and IV Corps from 1965 until Lon Nol's coup (003 §2 F003-3; EV003-2)
- **POS004-2** · vars: ARVN.effectiveness, US.unit_quality, US.political_tolerance · In this war the ARVN and the RF/PF carry modern carbines from 1964, and the 1967 M16 crisis and inquiry and the 1968–69 rearmament do not occur; from 1969 the historical army has caught up, and the remaining difference is the squad gun, the marksman and the practice (004 F004-6; §4.P2–P4)
- **POS004-3** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, LOG.distribution · Abundant American ammunition from 1964 deepens the RVNAF's dependence on volume of fire; the 1974 ration falls hardest on the squad gun, and the divisional hoards built against it are lost in the collapse of March 1975 (004 F004-15; §4.P6)
- **POS005-1** · vars: STRIKE.responsiveness, FIND.main_force, FIX.capability · GPS weapons change what dies at a measured coordinate, never what can be located; in this war the J's precision is decisive where the enemy holds still long enough to be measured, at the siege and the fixed crossing, and adds nothing against the main force under canopy or the infrastructure in the hamlets (005 §2 F005-1, F005-7, F005-21)
- **POS005-2** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, FIX.capability, US.political_tolerance · In this war the defence of besieged positions from 1965 rests on the B-52J and an American coordinate cell; it is far stronger while American air power is present and leaves the RVNAF more dependent on it when it goes (005 §2 F005-20)
- **POS005-4** · vars: TRAIL.capacity, TRAIL.tonnage_arriving · In this war the panhandle's fixed crossings were cut by the B-52J from April 1966, and Group 559 rebuilt the net as braided fords, causeways and pontoons with no single point of failure; from 1966 the Trail is more redundant than history's, and precision strikes on crossings are never counted as reductions in tonnage arriving (005 §4.P2; EV005-2, EV000-55)
- **POSCP01-2** · vars: ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.self_sufficiency · In this war the American lever was used to protect the Republic's honest institutions from its own governments and never to make the Republic own the instruments of the conventional war (coordinates, reconnaissance, guided weapons, ammunition stocks); the dependence deepened by memoranda 004 and 005 was never contested by the instrument that could have contested it (CP01 §3)
- **POS006-3** · vars: ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.self_sufficiency · The selected advisory corps deepens influence, not authority; its durable values are continuity across the American unit's relief and honest reporting, and a better adviser deepens the advised unit's dependence on American fire unless he hands over the radio, which works for artillery, the VNAF and medevac and not for the B-52J (006 F006-2, F006-17, F006-23)
- **POS007-1** · vars: ARVN.leadership, ARVN.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · In this war the ARVN's battalions from 1965–67 are commanded by officers a board chose on written criteria and two raters' reports, for eighteen months, with relief for cause; this puts ARVN effectiveness at the cap of the bands in 1966–68, and the enemy answers by declining the better battalion and attacking the unreformed unit beside it, so the gain appears as battalions not lost rather than in any metric (007 §4.P2; EV007-2, EV007-3)
- **POS007-4** · vars: US.unit_quality, US.casualties, POP.civilian_harm · American officer education from 1957 improves platoon and company leadership and saves American lives at a rate of perhaps one to three percent of small-unit deaths in 1965–69, below a band; it does not prevent My Lai or the late-war decay of discipline, which came from the command climate above the lieutenant (007 §4.P2, §4.P3; EV000-23)
- **POSMT01-1** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, VNAF.capability, ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.leadership · Rung (a) is reaffirmed after seven memoranda on its mechanism, not its date: every provision so far is American-owned and withdrawn by 1973, or works below the level of command at which 1972 and 1975 were decided, or was captured by the palace when the American lever lapsed in 1970–71; the rung will not move until a provision reaches an air arm the Republic owns, sustainment that survives the 1974 appropriation, or the choice of the corps commanders (MT01 M-12)
- **POSMT01-3** · vars: HANOI.will, PAVN.strength_south, ARVN.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · The date of the Republic's fall, 30 April 1975 within a window of about 27 April to the first days of May, is derived and not carried: it was set by Hanoi's resolution of 25 March to finish before the rains and by the 1st Corps' march, and only a delay of about three weeks or more in the collapse of I and II Corps would have moved it, by putting the assault into the rains; better ARVN units act on fights the PAVN bypasses and do not reach that threshold (MT01 M-12; EVMT01-4, EV000-96)
- **POSMT01-6** · vars: ARVN.desertion, ARVN.effectiveness, POP.displacement · The ARVN's corps dissolved in March 1975 because the soldiers' families lived beside their units in the path of the offensive and the men went to them; no reform of the officer corps or the battalions reaches this, and it absorbed the gains of memoranda 004, 006 and 007 in the last campaign (MT01 open search; EV000-94, EV000-95)
- **POS008-1** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, ADVISE.leverage, US.political_tolerance · A domestic arsenal, battery works and rebuild depot stretch the aid dollar in 1974–75 only if the RVNAF has been made to buy from them while American supply was free; this headquarters adopts a domestic share enforced by the Aid Compliance Board from 1965, and the stretch changes what the fiscal 1975 appropriation buys, not the vote (008 §2 F008-2, F008-20, F008-23)
- **POS008-2** · vars: POP.night_control, RFPF.effectiveness, STRIKE.responsiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · A radio kept on the air at the post supplies the means of calling help in POSTNA-2 and moves the post's binding constraint to the reaction and fire within range; the Front answers by attacking the relief and the posts that cannot call, and the radio's gain appears as attacks not made (008 §2 F008-1, F008-3, F008-6, F008-16)
- **POS008-3** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, US.political_tolerance, HANOI.will · In this war the Republic's own arsenal and battery works stretched the fiscal 1975 appropriation to about $850 million–$1 billion of history's and kept its ammunition and communications from going dark in 1974, but delayed the collapse of I and II Corps by days, not the three weeks that would have moved the date; domestic sustainment without an air arm the Republic owns and a choice of corps commanders does not move the rung (008 §4.P6, §4.N; EV000-89, EVMT01-4)
- **POS008-4** · vars: RFPF.effectiveness, POP.night_control, STRIKE.responsiveness · From 1967 the territorial post's first call is for fire, not men, after the Front's ambush of the relief at My Phuoc Tay; this makes the post cheaper to hold and keeps the platoon behind its wire, so that the post is held better and the hamlet outside it is not, and the call passes to Vietnamese district guns in 1970–71 (008 §4.P2, §4.P4; EV008-4, EV008-7)
- **POS008-5** · vars: GVN.corruption, ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.self_sufficiency · The Directorate of Defence Industry fell to the palace in February 1970 with the four other institutions built behind the American lever; its output and the domestic share survived because the Joint General Staff wanted them, and honest lot acceptance did not, costing perhaps a tenth to a fifth of the base's 1974 value (008 §4.P4; EV002-6)
- **POS009-1** · vars: ARVN.effectiveness, RFPF.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · Basic training changes how the fights the enemy accepts go and how many wounded live after them, never which fights he accepts; in this war the ARVN of 1964–65 stands a band above history on the course, the carbine and the educated lieutenant together, and the enemy answers the trained soldier with the mine, the sapper and the untrained target (009 §4.P1, §4.P2; EV002-2, EV009-2, EV009-4)
- **POS010-1** · vars: ARVN.effectiveness, RFPF.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · In this war every RVNAF and territorial NCO since 1957 has passed the course for his grade, and empty squads are given to corporals first class who passed the leader's course; this changes how squads and posts fight the fights the enemy accepts, never which fights he accepts, and the enemy answers by passing the units that keep the routine and attacking those that do not, so the gain appears as companies not destroyed and posts not attacked (010 F010-19, F010-25; EV010-3, EV010-4)
- **POS010-4** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, STRIKE.responsiveness · The American NCO course carries the habit of fixing the enemy and calling fire down to the ARVN squad; it is a strength the Republic owns only where the gun at the other end is Vietnamese, as at Long My, and a dependence everywhere else (010 F010-24; EV008-7)
- **POSCP02-1** · vars: ARVN.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · In this war the ARVN battalion of 1966–68 stands at the cap of the bands through four memoranda (007, 009, 010 and 004 before them), and the battalions broken in 1966–67 are about two-fifths to a half fewer than history's, a judgment whose factors overlap and whose upper bound is the "about half" of 010; any further provision on the battalion is measured in that running sum and not in the band, and none of it changes which fights the enemy accepts (CP02 §3, §5)
- **POSCP02-2** · vars: ENEMY.engagement_control, POP.civilian_harm, VCI.strength · Every provision since 004 that improved the RVNAF below the company was answered by the enemy moving his war to what the provision did not reach: the relief, the borrowed district, the mine in the hamlet, the untrained self-defence group; the provisions' gain in the army is paid for in part by the unprotected population, and every later provision touching the army or the posts names the target the enemy moves to and estimates the cost there (CP02 §1, §6; EV008-4, EV009-2, EV009-4, EV010-4)
- **REVR01-1** · reverses POSCP02-1 · vars: ARVN.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · The judgment of POSCP02-1 on the war stands: the ARVN battalions broken in 1966–67 are about two-fifths to a half fewer than history's, a judgment whose factors overlap and whose upper bound is the "about half" of 010, and none of it changes which fights the enemy accepts. What is reversed is its method: further provisions on the ARVN battalion are no longer measured outside the variable because the variable is capped. They are measured on the v1.0.6 scale, in the range of ARVN effectiveness and the facet they act on, and the running sum feeds that range (R01)
- **POS011-2** · vars: US.political_tolerance, ARVN.self_sufficiency · American military aid to the RVNAF is about $950 million for fiscal 1975, buying through the domestic stretch about what $1.2 billion bought historically, with supplementals of about $150 million in March and $175 million in May 1975 and about $800 million for fiscal 1976; the money reached fuel, aircraft and heavy rounds and saved perhaps 1,500–4,000 of the Republic's dead in 1974, and it never reached the soldier's pay or the artillery duel with the 130mm (011 F011-2, F011-21; EV000-89, EV000-91, EV011-2, EV000-97, EV011-3)
- **POS011-3** · vars: GVN.political_stability, ARVN.effectiveness, ARVN.desertion · Thieu refused the Dalat study on 11 March 1975 and gave no withdrawal order on 13–14 March, because he held the money and the President's message; the refusal cost half the Highland force and the 2nd Division and delayed the collapse of I and II Corps by three to five weeks, and in May he took the study's method for SOUTHERN WALL; the counter-directional finding is the mechanism of the gain (011 F011-20; EV000-94, EV000-95, EV011-3)
- **POS011-4** · vars: POP.civilian_harm, US.credibility_gap, US.unit_quality · The Son My massacre is removed by stipulation and isolated: there is no Peers inquiry, no Calley trial and no inquiry into the Americal Division's command climate, every other killing of civilians in Quang Ngai stands, and Son My's people live under the Front; the public's verdict on the war is unchanged because it was in before November 1969 (011 F011-5, F011-10, F011-11; EV000-46, EV000-63, EV000-72)
- **REV011-1** · reverses POSMT01-3 · vars: HANOI.will, PAVN.strength_south, ARVN.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · The method of POSMT01-3 stands: the date of the fall is derived from Hanoi's calendar, and only a delay of about three weeks or more in the collapse of I and II Corps moves it. What is reversed is the date. In this war the collapse came three to five weeks late, because Thieu gave no withdrawal order on 13–14 March 1975; the Politburo put the assault on Saigon back to the dry season of 1975–76, and the fall is expected between February and May 1976 (011; EVMT01-4, EV000-94, EV000-95)
- **POS012-3** · vars: INTL.allied_forces, POP.civilian_harm · In this war the Korean forces accepted combined operational control only with a countersignature and a national referral, which put Korean soldiers beyond the Republic's law; the Korean element of the task force was withdrawn after Hoa Thanh in April 1966 and Korean soldiers took no further part in targeting the infrastructure (012 EV012-3, EV012-5)
- **POS013-1** · vars: AIR.north_effect, TRAIL.tonnage_arriving, HANOI.will · In this war the air campaign against the North was run from Saigon from 2 March 1965 on the theater's own list, without zones around Hanoi or Haiphong and without pauses, and opened with a strike that destroyed the North's power, bulk fuel, great bridges, jet base and Haiphong's cranes in a week; it did not reduce the flow to the South beyond the record's trace, and it did not move Hanoi's will; the restrictions on bombing the North were never the war's binding constraint (013 F013-7, F013-18; EV013-1, EV013-3)
- **POS013-3** · vars: AIR.losses, AIR.north_defences · In this war Rolling Thunder lost about 810–880 aircraft over or near the North rather than 922: about 30–60 fewer in 1965, 40–90 fewer in 1966–67 and 30–40 more in the summer of 1968 over Hanoi; the VPAF fought from Chinese airfields from 1965, and Bolo destroyed three MiG-21s rather than seven (013 F013-17, F013-18; EV000-53, EVCP02-4)
- **POSCP03-1** · vars: STRIKE.responsiveness, PAVN.strength_south, TRAIL.tonnage_arriving · The unrestricted opening of the air war against the North in March 1965 disrupted the North's economy, air force and alliances more than any other act of the war and did not reach the war in the South: the South's needs were small, carried through Laos by labour, and the North replaced fuel and power with drums and diesels in a season, while the trucks Moscow sent in place of heavy plant went to the Trail (POSTNA-4, C013-1). The divisions held at home in 1965 were the North's home-defence divisions on history's course too, and no formation reaches the South late by more than weeks (CP03 §5, the user's question of 25 Nov 2026)
- **POS014-1** · vars: FIND.vci, VCI.strength, SANCT.cambodia · In this war a night raid force on the Front's senior apparatus from 1964 drove that apparatus out of the provinces it administered and across the Cambodian border by 1967, where no allied instrument could reach it; the raid force's falling yield from 1967 measures that success and not its failure, and the displacement is never reported as a reduction in the Front's organisation (014 §4.P2, F014-19, F014-21; EV014-5, EV014-7)
- **POS014-2** · vars: FIND.main_force, STRIKE.responsiveness · In this war reconnaissance teams produced the first coordinates measured from under the canopy, 134 of them in 1966–67; the record's limit on precision was location and remains location, and a team's coordinate is worth what can be struck in the hours before the target disperses (014 §4.P2, F014-11; EV014-4)
- **POS014-4** · vars: US.personnel_demand, ARVN.effectiveness · In this war a unit committed whole to one theater for eleven years held its headcount and spent its experience: about a quarter of its operators by the end of 1967 were selected after the war began, and its sustained rate was about half what its first months implied (014 §4.P2, F014-13; EV014-1, EV014-3)
- **POS015-1** · vars: RFPF.effectiveness, POP.night_control, STRIKE.responsiveness · In this war a gunship is over a post under attack within 15–30 minutes on a clear night in the net from January 1964; this supplies the reaction that arrives in the dark of POSTNA-2 for the post, not the hamlet, and the Front answers by attacking in cloud, beyond the net, from inside the hamlet and by day (015 F015-1, F015-5, F015-12)
- **POS015-2** · vars: VNAF.capability, ARVN.self_sufficiency, ADVISE.leverage · The VNAF's AC-130U wing, at strength from the end of 1969, is the first instrument of the air war the Republic owns and keeps after 1973; it works at the level of the territorial war and not of the command decisions of 1972 and 1975, and it flies on the appropriation (015 F015-4, F015-19)
- **POS015-3** · vars: RFPF.effectiveness, POP.night_control, STRIKE.responsiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · In this war from 1964 the Front does not assault a covered post on a clear night within the gunship net, and it moves its night attacks to the monsoon cloud, to the posts beyond the net and into the hamlets; on the coast of I and II Corps the monsoon nights are the Front's until the VNAF's radar gunships cover them from 1969 (015 EV015-1, EV015-2, EV015-4)
- **POS015-4** · vars: VNAF.capability, ARVN.self_sufficiency, POP.night_control · The VNAF's gunship wing holds the Delta's posts at night in 1973–75 and cannot fly over the PAVN's divisions, which bring their own air defence; it changes which posts the Republic holds and not which divisions it can stop, and it does not move the critical path of 1975 (015 EV015-8, EV000-91, EV000-95)
- **REVCP04-1** · reverses POS004-3 · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, LOG.distribution · The first half of POS004-3 stands: abundant American ammunition from 1964 deepened the RVNAF's dependence on volume of fire, and the 1974 ration fell hardest on the squad gun. What is reversed is the hoards' fate, because this war has no collapse of March 1975: the Hue hoard of about 3 million rounds was destroyed in place on 17 April (EV000-94), the hoards of I and II Corps were not abandoned in March and what the Highlands and Quang Ngai held went with them in April, the 18th Division held Xuan Loc through the rains on more ammunition than history's April could find (EV000-96), and the stocks of III and IV Corps remain the Republic's at the end of 1975 (CP04 §8; small-arms study Q-3)

## Memoranda that touch these variables

001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008, 009, 010, 011, 012, 013, 014, 015

Their cards are in `build/cards/`; read only the ones the area turns on, and grep for the rest.

## Provisions in those memoranda

- **P001a** · Land-to-the-Tiller Programme, 1964 (accelerated and enhanced): zero retention of tenanted rice land, free distribution to the present tiller, confirmation of Viet Minh and Viet Cong distributions, US-financed landlord compensation, and a fit-for-purpose aerial-photo titling apparatus · One national programme: about 1.0–1.2 million ha of tenanted land to about 850,000–950,000 families [E: Prosterman's 1960–61 tenancy census and the GAO's 1970 LTTT target of 1 million ha to 800,000 tenants] · spaces ~260 US personnel, of whom ~60 military spaces [E: USAID land and survey advisers in each province plus an Army engineer topographic detachment; the 1970s LTTT advisory staff was 31] · SECURE, SUBVERT · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 001
- **P001b** · GVN Anti-Corruption Programme with Enforcement Mechanism: an independent Commission Against Corruption on the Hong Kong ICAC model with powers of arrest, search, seizure and compelled asset declaration, a special anti-corruption court, an independent RVNAF pay-and-muster verification service, and a joint US–GVN Aid Compliance Board empowered to suspend aid to a command or ministry · One national commission of about 2,000 Vietnamese staff with about 320 US advisers, investigators and auditors [E: ICAC's 1,213 staff for a city of about 7 million, scaled for a country of about 15 million and an armed force of about 514,000] · spaces ~320 US personnel, of whom ~140 military spaces [E: Army CID agents, finance and audit officers and muster teams; the rest USAID, Treasury and GAO-trained civilians] · ADVISE, SUSTAIN, SECURE · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 001
- **P002a** · National Police Reform Programme, 1964: a resident rural constabulary with a police post in every village, a rebuilt Police Special Branch with sole charge of intelligence on the VC infrastructure, a Police Field Force raised two years early, a national identity and family census, a police pay and career statute, and judicial safeguards on arrest and detention · One national programme: the National Police grown from about 19,000–22,000 in January 1964 to about 70,000 by the end of 1966 and about 95,000 by the end of 1968, of whom about 24,000 rural police resident in villages and about 7,500 Special Branch [E: village and district counts of the period, the historical growth to 88,000 by 1970, and training throughput] · spaces ~520 US personnel, of whom ~150 military spaces [E: about 300 USAID Public Safety advisers against the historical 144 of December 1965, about 150 Army military police and CID training-team spaces, about 70 contractor technicians for the identity system]; about 40 British, Malaysian and Australian police advisers outside US spaces · SECURE, FIND, SUBVERT · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 002
- **P002b** · Provincial Administration Reform, 1964: merit-based selection of province and district chiefs by an independent Provincial Administration Selection Board, by competitive examination, assessment and vetting, with appointment from a ranked list, a guaranteed two-year tenure removable only for cause, an independent Inspectorate of Provincial Administration, a pay and allowance reform, and a mandatory course before posting · About 290 chief posts (44–45 province chiefs and 239–243 district chiefs) and about 330 deputy posts, filled by competition over 1964–65 [E: the province and district counts of the period, one deputy for administration in each province and district] · spaces ~90 US personnel, of whom ~30 military spaces [E: a small advisory staff to the Selection Board and the Inspectorate, assessment-centre specialists, and province senior advisers' share of the inspection work] · SECURE, ADVISE · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 002
- **P003a** · Lockheed Martin U-2S Dragon Lady (Block 20), 2026 configuration: ASARS-2A synthetic aperture radar with moving-target indication, SYERS-2C multispectral electro-optical and infrared camera, ASIP signals intelligence payload, with a deployable ground exploitation station · 2 aircraft [U] · spaces ~220 [E: four to five pilots and a mobile-crew cell, about 90 maintainers and life-support technicians, about 20 contractor field engineers, and an exploitation and SIGINT cell of about 100 in shifts] · FIND, STRIKE, INTERDICT · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 003
- **P003b** · Northrop Grumman RQ-4B Global Hawk Block 40, 2026 configuration: MP-RTIP active electronically scanned array radar with simultaneous ground moving-target indication and synthetic aperture imaging, with a Launch and Recovery Element and a Mission Control Element · 4 aircraft [U] · spaces ~380 [E: six to seven three-person mission crews for one continuous orbit, an LRE detachment, about 140 maintainers and contractor technicians, and a GMTI and radar-imagery exploitation cell of about 150 in shifts] · FIND, INTERDICT, STRIKE · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 003
- **P004a** · M4A1 carbine with the Upper Receiver Group – Improved (URG-I: Geissele Automatics upper, Daniel Defense 14.5-inch 1:7 barrel, mid-length gas, Mk16 13.5-inch M-LOK rail, SureFire SF4P flash hider) and Aimpoint CompM5 2 MOA red-dot sight, firing M855A1 5.56mm, 2026 configuration · All rifles and carbines of US forces and the RVNAF, and all RF/PF [U]: a first increment of about 600,000 carbines and sights in 1964, rising to about 1.7–1.9 million cumulative by 1972 [E: RVNAF 514,000 in 1964 and about 1,048,000 in 1971–72 per S9, US strength rising to about 540,000 at peak, plus a 10% float] · spaces ~250 [E: about 120 new-equipment training spaces in the first year, about 80 small-arms and optics repair technicians at the depots, and about 50 added small-arms advisers to the RF/PF training centres; no troop ceiling is set, but each space still costs] · SECURE, FIX, ADVISE, SUSTAIN · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 004
- **P004b** · Knight's Armament Company M110A2 7.62mm semi-automatic rifle (20-inch free-floated match barrel, integral suppressor, 12-inch M-LOK handguard, collapsible stock) with SIG Sauer TANGO6T 1-6x24mm first-focal-plane illuminated variable-power scope, firing M118LR and M80A1 7.62mm, issued one per infantry squad as the designated marksman's rifle, 2026 configuration · One per US and ARVN infantry squad [U]: about 5,000 rifles and scopes in 1964, about 13,000 cumulative by 1972 [E: about 120 ARVN, Ranger, Airborne and Marine battalions of about 36 squads in 1964 rising to about 180 by 1972, plus up to about 112 US Army and Marine manoeuvre battalions at the 1968–69 peak, plus a 10% float] · spaces ~120 [E: marksman instructor teams of about 60 at the training centres and about 60 match-rifle and scope armourers; the marksmen themselves are squad members already counted] · FIX, SECURE, STRIKE · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 004
- **P004c** · FN America M249 5.56mm light machine gun (PIP-standard, 465mm barrel, collapsible stock) with SIG Sauer TANGO6T 1-6x24mm scope (DWLR-556 reticle), firing linked M855A1 from 200-round pouches or STANAG magazines, at squad level in US and ARVN infantry in place of the BAR and the squad's automatic weapon, 2026 configuration · At squad level in US and ARVN infantry [U]: about 5,200 guns in 1964, about 17,000–19,000 cumulative by 1972 [E: one per ARVN squad in place of its BAR, two per Army squad and three per Marine squad in place of the fire teams' automatic rifles, on the battalion counts of P004b, plus a 10% float] · spaces ~100 [E: machine-gun instructor teams of about 40 and about 60 armourers for barrels, gas systems and feed trays; the gunners are squad members already counted] · FIX, SECURE · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 004
- **P005a** · Boeing B-52J Stratofortress, programme-of-record configuration: B-52H airframe re-engined with eight Rolls-Royce F130 turbofans (Commercial Engine Replacement Program), Raytheon AN/APQ-188 AESA radar (Radar Modernization Program), digital cockpit displays, 1760 Internal Weapons Bay Upgrade, GPS-aided navigation and the H's electronic-warfare suite, replacing every B-52 one for one · Every B-52 in the USAF inventory replaced one for one [U]: about 600 airframes in 1964 across SAC [E: 744 B-52s built, less attrition and retirements of early B and C models], of which the force committed to Southeast Asia follows the historical deployment: 30 in mid-1965 [H], about 50–70 through 1966–67 [E: sortie rates of about 800 a month by mid-1967 per S9], about 90–100 from early 1968 [E: 1,800 sorties a month from February 1968 per S9], 210 at the 1972 peak [S9] · spaces 0 in RVN for the bomber force itself [E: Arc Light flew from Guam, U-Tapao and Okinawa]; about 40 in RVN for an enlarged Arc Light liaison and target-coordinate cell at MACV and Seventh Air Force [E: the historical ARC LIGHT liaison element plus a coordinate-mensuration team]; outside RVN, maintenance manpower about 10–20% below the historical B-52 force [E: F130 needs no off-wing overhaul per S4, five-man crew per S2 against the D's six] · STRIKE, INTERDICT, FIX, SUSTAIN · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 005
- **P005b** · GBU-31 Joint Direct Attack Munition, 2,000 lb class: GBU-31(V)1/B on the Mk 84 general-purpose bomb and GBU-31(V)3/B on the BLU-109 penetrator, Boeing GPS-aided INS tail kit, with FMU-152 or equivalent programmable fuze, 2026 configuration · Supplied with the B-52J force at realistic production rates [U]: about 8,000–12,000 kits a year from 1964 for the bomber force [E: about a third of a JDAM production line of 25,000–40,000 kits a year, the rest going to the GBU-38 and to stocks] · spaces ~60 in RVN [E: a coordinate-mensuration and weaponeering cell at MACV J-2 and Seventh Air Force working in shifts]; kit build-up and loading crews of about 150–250 at Andersen and U-Tapao outside RVN [E: munitions maintenance squadron increments] · STRIKE, INTERDICT · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 005

## Errata affecting those memoranda

### E01
# E01 — Memorandum 003: the RQ-4B and U-2S work with GPS and satellite links, under the standing condition of 23 Nov 2026
memos: 003
location: memos/003/part1.md — the reading of "granted" in the opening paragraphs; §1.1 D1 (unit organisation) and D6 (architecture and geometry) for P003a, with every later passage that limits it to its line-of-sight tether; §1.2 D1 (configuration, unit organisation), D6 (architecture, geometry, lost link), D7 (basing), every later passage that limits it to line of sight or to the positioning array, and the card figures and negative specification for P003b
wrong: "In January 1964 there is no GPS, and there will be none for fourteen years; there are no military communications satellites in orbit [H]. … My reading, therefore, is that each RQ-4 is delivered with what it minimally needs to take off, navigate and land without satellites — a ground-based local positioning array at its home runway to stand in for differential GPS, and an inertial navigation solution corrected in flight against radar imagery of surveyed ground — and that its control and its data travel only by line-of-sight link"; card P003b: "Links: line of sight only, about 200–250 nm from a terminal" and "Navigation: inertial with radar map-matching and a local positioning array at the home runway"; negative specification: "within about 250 nm of Bien Hoa or Da Nang"; P003a D6: "A 2026 U-2 in the Middle East would also pass data beyond line of sight by satellite; in 1964 it cannot, because no satellite exists to carry it [H]", with northern collection "hours after the event, not minutes".
correct: By standing condition, the GPS and military SATCOM constellations are present from the campaign's opening [U: standing condition, set 23 Nov 2026; recorded in rules/CONFIG.toml [conditions]]. Both provisions therefore arrive and fly exactly as they fly in 2026, and the Part 1 reading is withdrawn. (1) P003b navigates by GPS-aided inertial navigation and takes off and lands on differential GPS corrections from its own Launch and Recovery Element [M003·S7]; there is no site-specific positioning array, and the "array damaged by a mortar round" failure mode does not exist. Any runway its LRE kit is set up on will serve. (2) P003b is controlled and passes its data both by line of sight and by satellite [M003·S6] [M003·S7]. Its reach is set by its endurance and the threat, not by a ground terminal: it can hold an orbit over the Red River delta, the Gulf of Tonkin, the whole of the Laotian panhandle and Cambodia, and the Mission Control Element need not sit beside the runway. A lost line-of-sight link falls back to satellite control. The Da Nang relay terminal is not needed for control; Da Nang remains a recovery alternate and a direct line-of-sight data receiver. (3) P003a passes SIGINT, radar and electro-optical data beyond line of sight by Ku-band satellite through the dorsal-pod satellite datalinks (Senior Span, Senior Spur) when out of tether range [S13], so northern collection reaches the ground station in near real time, not after landing [S14]. (4) Nothing else in Part 1 changes: the sensors, altitudes, endurance, canopy blindness, the SA-2 threat, personnel spaces and the find-and-fix limits stand as written. (5) The condition gives the constellations, not user equipment: the historical 1964–75 force has no GPS receivers or satellite terminals (A3a). Coordinates these aircraft generate are GPS-accurate; the aircraft, artillery and ground units that must use them navigate and bomb by the period's methods (map grids, LORAN, TACAN, radar bombing).
source: The user's message of 23 Nov 2026 setting the condition (not a provision; no memorandum); Part 1's own sources S6 and S7 for the RQ-4's satellite and GPS architecture; memos/003/sources.md S13 and S14 for the U-2's satellite datalinks.
consequences: No chapter carries or relies on the Part 1 reading (memorandum 003 has not reached Part 3), so no revision is needed. Memorandum 003 Part 2 is written on the corrected basis. Any later memorandum loading card 003 loads this erratum.

### E02
# E02 — Memorandum 001: satellite navigation is available to the land survey, under the standing condition of 23 Nov 2026
memos: 001
location: memos/001/part1.md §1.1 D3 ("How it learns it", aerial photography) and the card figures for the land programme
wrong: "in 1964 there are no navigation satellites to use: the first GPS satellite is fourteen years away [H]. Every block of photography must therefore be tied to ground control points surveyed by optical total station from the French triangulation network"; card: "no satellite navigation in 1964, so ground control by optical survey [H]".
correct: By standing condition, the GPS constellation is present from the campaign's opening [U: standing condition, set 23 Nov 2026; recorded in rules/CONFIG.toml [conditions]]. The 2026 camera is designed for direct georeferencing with satellite navigation and an inertial system [M001·S10], and the provision's own 2026 survey equipment uses it; ground control is by GNSS-surveyed points rather than optical traverse from the French network. The photography schedule (about three months for the rice lands) and the titling rate stand as written: the titling rate was bound by security, not by survey [M001].
source: The user's message of 23 Nov 2026 setting the condition; memo 001's own source S10.
consequences: None in the war. The chapters' titling pace rests on village access by day [M001], which the condition does not touch; no revision is needed. The topographic detachment's ground-control workload falls; its other tasks stand.

### E03
# E03 — Memorandum 010: the NCO education grant includes the Regional and Popular Forces
memos: 010
location: memos/010/part1.md — the preamble's third reading ("'ARVN' means the regular forces … The Regional and Popular Forces are not named … Their sergeants keep the schooling history gave them"); §1.2 (P010b) D1 ("What it is not", quantity, organisation), D2 (instructor and US space costs), D7 (reach), D13 (margin), D14 and the card negative specification ("It does not reach the Regional and Popular Forces"), D16 and the card verdict ("It does not reach the territorial forces"), and the card figures for P010b; §1.1 (P010a) D14 and the card negative specification ("It does not reach the Regional and Popular Forces, or the officers"), as to the Regional and Popular Forces
wrong: "Third, 'ARVN' means the regular forces … The Regional and Popular Forces are not named, and memorandum 009 needed the grant to name them before it reached them. Their sergeants keep the schooling history gave them"; P010b card: "It does not reach the Regional and Popular Forces. Their NCOs, who led the platoons that held the hamlets, keep the schooling history gave them; the territorial war's sergeants are unchanged."
correct: The grant includes the Regional and Popular Forces [U: the user's ruling of 24 Nov 2026 in the memorandum 010 thread, "No, RF/PF is included"]. P010b covers every NCO of the RVNAF regular forces and of the Regional and Popular Forces (the Civil Guard and Self-Defense Corps before 1964) from 1957, on the same sequence of courses and the same gates. (1) Courses: the territorial NCO takes the same Basic, Advanced, Senior and Master Leader Courses as the regular NCO [U]; the Basic Leader Course is taught to RF and PF corporals and squad leaders at the RF/PF training centres (37 cut to 19 under the Central Training Command per M009·S12) with an RF/PF wing at the Nha Trang academy for the senior courses [E: the regular forces' arrangement applied to the territorial school system]. The PF platoon leader, a sergeant or sergeant first class leading a platoon of about 35 men [M009·S11], holds the Advanced Leader Course before he takes the platoon. (2) Quantity: RF and PF NCOs number about 10,000–15,000 in 1957, about 25,000–40,000 on 1 Jan 1964 and about 55,000–80,000 at the 1969 peak [E: an NCO share of 12–20% of a Civil Guard and Self-Defense Corps of about 86,000 in 1959 per M009·S10 and of 391,000 RF and PF in 1969 per M009·S11, at four to seven NCOs in a 35-man PF platoon and 15–20 in a 123-man RF company per M009·S10]. The territorial forces add about 6,000–10,000 course completions a year in 1957–63, 12,000–20,000 in 1964–67 and 20,000–35,000 at the 1968–70 peak [E: same basis]. The combined P010b throughput is therefore about 14,000–24,000 a year in 1957–63, 27,000–45,000 in 1964–67 and 50,000–80,000 at the peak. (3) Cost: about 500–1,000 more Vietnamese instructors before 1964 and 1,500–2,500 more at the peak, drawn from RF and regular NCOs [E: the 2026 ratio of one to 12–16]; about 60–120 more US personnel in RVN, of whom 50–110 military spaces, for advisory teams at the RF/PF centres [E: two to five advisers at each of 19–37 centres]. P010b's US cost becomes about 210–420 personnel, of whom about 180–380 military spaces; no troop ceiling is set (CONFIG). (4) Reach and preconditions: the territorial NCO's school is near his province, but his release depends on the province and district chiefs who controlled RF/PF manning [M009]; the gate gives them the same incentive it gives the regular commander. The territorial NCO's family lives in or near the hamlet he guards (DIRMT01-9), so his absence at a course leaves the post a leader short and his family where the enemy can reach it. (5) Effect: the gap the course closes is widest here. Historically, PF leadership training ran up to 60% behind programme in 1964 and its quotas were never filled [M010·S9]. Under the grant every PF squad and platoon leader holds the course for his grade, and the PF platoon in the hamlet at night is led by a sergeant who has been taught to site its position, post its listening posts, control its fire and hold it together until the reaction force arrives. P010b pushes RFPF.effectiveness +1 in addition to its regular-force pushes [X-010]. (6) Withdrawn: the negative-specification bullets for P010b and P010a that say the provision does not reach the Regional and Popular Forces, and the clause of the P010b verdict "It does not reach the territorial forces". Everything else in Part 1 stands, including the double drain of D2, which this widens: the RF/PF centres' instructors come from the same thin layer of senior territorial NCOs.
source: The user's message of 24 Nov 2026 in the memorandum 010 thread; memos/009/sources.md S10–S12 for the territorial forces' strengths, organisation and training centres; memos/010/sources.md S9 for the 1964 PF leadership training shortfall.
consequences: None in the war: memorandum 010 has not reached Part 3, so no chapter carries the Part 1 reading and no revision is needed. The manifest's P010b entry and the standing condition nco_education_1957 in rules/CONFIG.toml are corrected to include the Regional and Popular Forces. Memorandum 010's Parts 2 and 3 are written on the corrected basis. Any later memorandum loading card 010 loads this erratum.

### E04
# E04 — The Regional Forces at STILL WATER and Bau Bang carried BARs, not M249s
memos: 006, 007, 009
location: history/chapters/P1.md EV006-2 (Operation STILL WATER, written by memorandum 006, memos/006/amend.md), the paragraph on the operation's plan; history/chapters/P2.md EV007-3 (Operation OPEN ROAD, the Bau Bang convoy paragraph written by memorandum 009, memos/009/amend.md)
wrong: EV006-2: "the Regional Forces companies of Hoc Mon and Go Vap, with M4A1 carbines and their M249s, held the cordons at night"; EV007-3: "the second company, at the rear, put its two M249s into the treeline within the first two minutes [M009] [X-009]"
correct: EV006-2: the Regional Forces companies of Hoc Mon and Go Vap held the cordons "with M4A1 carbines and the BARs that the territorials kept as their automatic rifles" [M004]; EV007-3: the rear company "put its BARs into the treeline within the first two minutes", and the Regional Forces never drew the squad gun [M004]. The Regional and Popular Forces received the M4A1 carbine of P004a but not the M249 of P004c: P004c's negative specification reads "The Regional and Popular Forces do not receive it: the outpost keeps its BAR" (memos/004/part1.md §1, P004c, "What it is not") [M004], and the province chiefs' diversion of squad guns to their RF posts was abandoned and the guns recalled to the squads (EC004-10, memos/004/part2.md) [M004]. EV000-42 already keeps the rule: the 311th RF Company at Cai Lay had "one squad gun lent by the 7th Division". No later memorandum issued the M249 to the territorial forces; memorandum 008's arsenal provision still lists the Browning Automatic Rifle "still with the territorial forces" (memos/008/part1.md) [M008].
source: Study ST02, us-and-arvn-small-arms-and-individual-weapons-ag (studies/us-and-arvn-small-arms-and-individual-weapons-ag.md), Questions for the record, Q-1 · ERRATUM; checked against memos/004/part1.md (P004c negative specification), memos/004/part2.md (EC004-10), history/chapters/P3.md (EV000-42) and memos/008/part1.md.
consequences: Both errors reached the war, so revision R04 corrects the two events in history/chapters/P1.md and P2.md. Neither event's outcome rested on the squad gun. STILL WATER was a police and Special Branch operation in which the RF companies held cordons; nothing in it turns on the cordon's automatic weapon. At Bau Bang memorandum 009 credited the lower RF losses (about 32 dead rather than about 40) to the six-week territorial course, which taught the men to leave the trucks on the far side, fight from the ditch and return fire in pairs [M009] [X-009]; that judgment stands with BARs, whose 20-round magazine gave the rear company a shorter burst of covering fire than a belt-fed gun would have. No end vector, position or end state changes. The small arms study's Bau Bang passage (§ on Phase II) is corrected by R04's study entry. Any later pack that loads the cards of memoranda 006, 007 or 009 loads this erratum.

### E05
# E05 — The National Police and the Police Field Force keep their historical weapons
memos: 002
location: memos/002/part1.md §1.1 (P002a) D3 · Weapons and payload, the paragraph "**Weapons.**"
wrong: "the 2026 configuration replaces the carbine with the M4 carbine and adds a 12-gauge pump shotgun of Remington 870 class to each constable's equipment, because the policeman's weapon must be good enough to defend the post against a probe and no better, or he becomes a soldier [U]. Each post has an M60 machine gun for the post's defence [U], where the historical police had at best an M1919A4 [S1]. The Field Force platoon carries M16-family rifles, an M79 grenade launcher and a machine gun, with 24 shotguns in each company's pool [S5] [U: M16A1 rather than the historical Garands and carbines from the start], and no mortars [S5]."
correct: The National Police and the Police Field Force keep their historical weapons [U: the user's ruling of 25 Nov 2026, "Police keep historical weapons for now"]. The village constable carries the M1 or M2 carbine, or a pump shotgun of the period where his station issues one, and a .38 revolver (the Smith & Wesson Model 10 or the M1917), with the M1911A1 pistol for officers and the M3A1 sub-machine gun in station armouries [M002·S1]. The post has no 2026 weapon: its only automatic weapon, where it has one, is the automatic rifle of the period, with at best an M1919A4 [M002·S1], which is what memorandum 002's own Part 2 counts in a post ("about ten carbines and an automatic rifle", §2 Part B, Perverse effect) [M002]. The Police Field Force carries the M1 and M2 carbine, the M1918A2 automatic rifle and the M79 grenade launcher (memos/006/part1.md, P006 PRU weapons: "what the Police Field Force carries in this war") [M006], with the company's pool of 24 shotguns [M002·S5]. The rearmament of memorandum 004 does not reach them (P004a negative specification; F004-1; the P002a interaction line in memos/004/part2.md) [M004]. The clause on the policeman's weapon being "good enough to defend the post against a probe and no better, or he becomes a soldier" stands as the reason a constable is not armed as a soldier; it no longer justifies a 2026 weapon. Everything else in D3 stands. "For now": a later provision may rearm the police; until one does, these are its weapons.
source: Study ST03, us-and-arvn-small-arms-and-individual-weapons-ag (studies/us-and-arvn-small-arms-and-individual-weapons-ag.md), Questions for the record, Q-6 · ERRATUM, which found memorandum 002 Part 1 at odds with memorandum 004 and the chapters and left the choice to the user because P002a's weapons were stipulated [U]; the user's ruling of 25 Nov 2026 in the project chat. Checked against memos/002/part2.md and part3.md, memos/004/part2.md (F004-1, the P002a interaction line), memos/004/manifest.toml (links note), memos/006/part1.md and memos/006/amend.md, history/chapters/P1.md (EV002-2, EV004-1) and the study's own tables.
consequences: None in the war. The error was confined to memorandum 002 Part 1's D3 paragraph and never reached a chapter, an end vector, a card, a register or the end state: P002a's card (figures, negative specification, denial, verdict) states no weapons, memorandum 002's own Parts 2 and 3 already wrote the posts as stores of "M1 carbines and a radio" and "about ten carbines and an automatic rifle", with Long Dinh on 3 October 1964 "a gift of nine carbines to the Front's guerrillas" (F002-8), and every later record carries the historical weapons: memorandum 004 (P004a does "not cover the National Police, the Police Field Force"; F004-1, the attacks move to "the men who still carry carbines"), EV002-2 ("ten constables carrying the carbines of 1950"), EV004-1 (a third of the 290,000 old weapons handed down to the police, the Combat Youth and the militia over MACV's objection), memorandum 006 (the PRUs and the Field Force with carbines, M1918A2s and M79s), and the small arms study (ST03), whose table of history's weapons and of this war's rearmament leaves the police unchanged. Because the ruling keeps the version the war was written on, every outcome that rested on the police's weapons stands as written and needs no re-reading: the Front's choice of the police posts and the constables as the soft target from December 1964 (F004-1, F009-6), the roughly 300 weapons lost with the police posts by July 1965, nearly all of them carbines, and the constables' losses of 1964–65 (EV002-2) [X-004]. No revision is run, and no event, end vector, position or end state changes. Study ST03's Q-6 is answered by this erratum; the next checkpoint marks it RESOLVED. One related point is noted and not ruled on here: memorandum 002 gives the Field Force "no mortars" [M002·S5], while the Long An passage that memoranda 002 and 006 staged in their amend files gave the two Long An Field Force companies of November 1965 "60mm mortars" [X-002]; the current chapters no longer carry that clause, so nothing in the war rests on it. Any later pack that loads memorandum 002's card loads this erratum.

## Standing directives

- **DIRCP01-1** · In each Part 3, take at least one causal chain from an earlier memorandum whose later links fall in a phase this memorandum revises, and test it against the war as now written; where the new provision or free play makes it resolve differently, say so in the chain review and let it (every chain in memoranda 001–005 resolved as predicted, which is more likely tidiness than foresight)
- **DIRCP01-2** · A war-wide figure for lives saved, or any war-wide count built from a rate, must be shown at work in at least two dated events in the chapters before a later memorandum repeats it; until then it is cited as a judgment resting on its rate, with the rate named (CP01 calibration of the [X-004] lives-saved figure)
- **DIRMT01-1** · In every §4.N, state the date of the Republic's fall as its own estimate, separately from the rung: a window, the mechanisms in the cumulative force that pull it earlier and those that pull it later, and which dominate and why; "on the historical timeline" may be written only as the conclusion of that test, and a change of date is reported as a change of date and does not by itself move the rung between (a) and (b) while the ladder's overlap stands (the historical fall, twenty-five months after the last American combat troops left, satisfies the words of rung (b), and seven memoranda have kept (a) and (b) apart by the date alone)
- **DIRMT01-2** · In every §4.N, carry a running sum of the sub-band estimates that all memoranda so far have made on the same variable (American dead, ARVN battalions not lost, and the like), tagged as exercise judgments with their rates named, and say whether the sum crosses a band; and treat the American aid appropriation of 1974 and the refusal of April 1975 as events a provision can change, not as history to be carried (each memorandum judged its own saving of American lives alone, and the 1974 vote was never examined)
- **DIRMT01-3** · Where a chapter's end vector returns a variable to the historical state from a non-zero band in the phase before, the chapter must contain the dated events that produce the convergence; and in every memorandum that revises Phase VI, state in the phase's analysis the Republic's state at the end of 1974, before the last offensive, because the phase's end vector is measured after the fall and cannot record anything the fall erased (Phase V returned four countryside variables to history with no sentence on the countryside, and Phase VI's vector is blind by construction)
- **DIRMT01-4** · Where a memorandum alters an event and keeps its historical outcome, name what absorbs the difference (the enemy's choice to bypass or decline, a decision above the level the provision reached, an external fixed by law or by another government) and show it in the event; "as historically" is a conclusion, never a mechanism (in Phase VI at least six altered events in the last campaign restore the historical outcome by statement)
- **DIRMT01-5** · Where a perverse effect or a capture undoes a gain, state the net in both directions with its weight, and where several provisions' institutions fall to the same mechanism in the same years, judge them together before judging each alone (four institutions from four memoranda fall to the lapse of the American lever in 1970–71, each judged alone, and every memorandum closes on the gain undone)
- **DIRMT01-6** · The next memorandum or review whose Part 3 revises Phase V or VI states the PAVN's 1972 losses in this war against the historical figure and the rebuilding time that follows, before writing 1973–75 (memorandum 005 made the measured sieges the enemy's worst battles; Phase V keeps the historical losses and Phase VI the historical rebuilding)
- **DIRMT01-7** · Every memorandum whose Part 3 revises Phase V or VI tests its effects against the critical path of 1975 (the palace's orders of 13–14 March, the 1st Corps' march against the rains, and Minh's surrender) and states whether any mechanism could delay the collapse of I and II Corps by about three weeks, the threshold beyond which the assault falls into the rains; effects on fights the PAVN could bypass are reported as such (the date of the fall was carried for seven memoranda without its critical path ever being stated)
- **DIRMT01-8** · Every memorandum touching the countryside states its effect separately for the Delta, the coastal lowlands of I and II Corps, the Highlands and their peoples, and the Saigon belt, and names a place in each where the effect is shown or says why there is none (the Delta was written as a footnote, the Montagnards appear twice and FULRO never, and Binh Dinh vanished from the record after 1967)
- **DIRMT01-9** · Every provision touching the reliability of the ARVN or the territorial forces addresses the soldier's family: where it lives, what his pay buys after inflation, and what happens to it when the unit moves or the front gives way (the corps of 1975 dissolved toward their families, and no memorandum had treated them)
- **DIRMT01-10** · The enemy's decisions have authors: in each memorandum name the body or commander who took the enemy's decision of G3, and distinguish Hanoi, the B-2 Front and COSVN, and the regional fronts where they differed; treat the Soviet and Chinese supply as variables with their own politics (COSVN vanishes from the record after 1971, the Phuoc Long argument is told as one mind, and the Soviet deliveries of 1974 are absent)
- **DIRMT01-11** · Every memorandum touching the countryside or the RVNAF states its effect on rice (production, procurement and the Front's take) and on the piaster and the soldier's pay, with at least one dated event (rice appears eleven times in Phase II and once in 1972–75, the years the economy decided)
- **DIRCP02-1** · At each checkpoint, consolidate a chapter over the limit in two steps: first merge minor historical events into summary events, then merge each memorandum's own minor NEW events in that phase into one summary per memorandum, keeping every fact a later memorandum or position cites by event number; and every memorandum's §4 adds to a phase's overview and ending only one paragraph, replacing rather than appending where an earlier memorandum's paragraph states the same variable (CP02 consolidation of P1 and P2, still about 7,600 and 9,300 words over the limit after the first step)
- **DIRCP02-2** · In each Part 3 the chain taken under DIRCP01-1 must be one written by another memorandum whose terminal event this memorandum did not write; C006-4, whose terminal link no chapter carries, is the first such chain for any memorandum revising Phase V (17 of 19 chains in memoranda 006–010 resolved as their authors predicted)
- **DIRCP02-3** · Where a provision acts on a variable already at the cap of the bands in a phase, the memorandum states its increment in the running sum of DIRMT01-2 with the factors it multiplies and how they overlap, and names the target the enemy moves to in answer (POSCP02-2); a product of overlapping judgments is reported as a range with its upper bound marked (CP02 calibration of the battalions-not-broken figure)
- **DIRR01-1** · DIRCP02-3's rule for a variable "already at the cap of the bands" lapses, because the scale has no cap short of a different war: a provision that acts on such a variable re-judges its range, and the range of the facet it acts on, and the running sums of DIRMT01-2 now say which part of that range they support rather than whether they cross a band; the rest of DIRCP02-3 stands, the target the enemy moves to in answer is still named, and a product of overlapping judgments is still reported as a range with its upper bound marked (the user's change of scale, 24 Nov 2026; R01)
- **DIRR01-2** · A range marked "converted" is the old band restated, not a judgment: it is never cited as a judgment of the war, and every memorandum or checkpoint whose evidence bears on a converted entry, or on one of the four entries converted from the cap, re-judges it with a confidence and a note (R01's mechanical conversion of the end vectors)
- **DIRR01-3** · Where a variable has facets, §2 names the facet a provision acts on, and every revised phase that judges a facet names the parent's binding facet and says why it binds; the parent is never the average of its facets, and a gain on one facet is not reported as a gain on the parent unless the binding facet moved (the user's point of 24 Nov 2026 that "ARVN effectiveness" does not discriminate between urban combat, combined arms, anti-armor and the rest)
- **DIRR02-1** · A study describes the war and never changes it: no study adds, alters or cancels an event or moves the end state, and where a study finds the record inconsistent it records a question for an erratum or a checkpoint rather than settling it (the user's design of 24 Nov 2026; R02)
- **DIRR02-2** · Every memorandum whose variables a study covers is written against that study: Part 2 judges its pushes against the study's values and says plainly when the provision's effect contradicts the study and which should give way, and Part 3 records what changed in the area in the study's entry (R02)
- **DIRR02-3** · A study's value is never cited as a measurement: study values are exercise judgments on the R01 scale, an indicator a study gives carries its own provenance, and a figure the study generates carries the X-tag of its study run (X-ST01 and so on) forever (A13a; R02)
- **DIRR03-1** · Every value and every push is written in its variable's natural unit (schema/VARIABLES.toml, v1.0.8): this war's figure beside history's where history's is known, otherwise the difference from history in the unit or as a percentage of history's figure, and a note that says what the figure means on the ground; a claim that cannot be put in its unit is not yet a judgment (the user's ruling of 25 Nov 2026 that the −10..+10 scale is meaningless; R03)
- **DIRR03-2** · A memorandum or checkpoint that judges a headline entry researches history's figure for it where it can and enters `hist` and `src`; an `[E: basis]` estimate of history's figure is allowed with its basis stated, and an unresearched figure is never stated from memory (R03; CLAUDE.md "read; never recall")
- **DIRR03-3** · A memorandum re-judges, in units, every unjudged headline entry among its own dependencies when its evidence bears on it, not only the variables it pushes (CP03 §3: night control sat converted through three memoranda that broke the infrastructure it depends on)
- **DIRCP03-1** · A dedicated consolidation run brings Phases I and II under the chapter limit before the next checkpoint: minor events merged into summary events by the CANCELLED/NEW rule, per-memorandum paragraphs merged by subject, every fact a later memorandum or position relies on kept, and successive restatements of one figure given once with its parts (CP03 §2: Phase III's three restatements of the first phase's dead)
- **DIRCP03-2** · A push or judgment on enemy strength (PAVN.strength_south, VC.main_force, VC.local_force) names the formations it moves and by how many months, and is tested against the chapters' order of battle before it is entered (CP03 §5: memorandum 013's divisions held at home)
- **DIRCP03-3** · A memorandum that improves FIND.vci states what the improvement tells the allies about the enemy's main forces and the timing of their offensives, and what it does not; files on the political organisation warn of where, not when (POSCP03-2)
- **DIRCP04-1** · A memorandum or review that cites a running sum or a settled figure takes it from the latest entry in `history/positions.md`, checking first for a REV entry that reverses it; a superseded figure is never carried forward (CP04 §8: memoranda 014 and 015 began their sum of American lives from POSMT01-5, which REV011-2 had reversed)
- **DIRCP04-2** · The ARVN battalions not broken in 1966–67 are stated once in the record, as about two-fifths to a half fewer than history's, at low confidence and more likely near two-fifths (REVR01-1, POSCP04-1's method): the consolidation run replaces Phase II's three successive increments ([X-007], [X-009], [X-010]) with that one statement, and no later memorandum adds an increment without checking its cases against the earlier ones (CP04 Part 1 §5)
- **DIRCP04-3** · A memorandum that removes or replaces a historical system greps every chapter for it, including the phases it does not revise, and either alters each event that names it or states in that phase's null why the event stands (CP04 Part 1 §2: the Spectre at Commando Hunt and the AC-119 at An Loc survived memorandum 015 in phases it did not revise)
- **DIRCP04-4** · A passage on the experience of the war (CHECKPOINT step 7, and any memorandum or study that writes one) is a narrative from one person's point of view: one named person, one place, one night or day, told in scene and in order, with what that person sees, hears, decides and does not know, and without the record's labels, IDs or provision names in the narrative itself; the claim it tests and what the scene shows about it follow in at most two sentences after the scene; a paragraph that restates the analysis with a name attached does not meet the step (the user's ruling of 25 Nov 2026 on CP04 Part 1 §6)
- **DIRR05-1** · Employment concepts that a later memorandum uses are cited by family, not re-invented under a new number: the committee hunt (EC006-1, EC006-4, EC012-7, EC012-8, EC014-1, EC014-2), the named offer (EC006-2, EC012-10), lists in the contested belt (EC012-9 the raid into the contested belt, and the abandoned EC001-4, EC006-12, EC012-11 and EC002-9), the visible American hand (abandoned: EC001-10, EC006-13, EC006-15, EC007-8, EC009-8, EC010-10), the panhandle watch (EC003-5, EC015-3, EC014-4, EC005-7), the night net and its handover (EC008-7, EC015-1, EC015-8, EC008-10, EC006-10) and the wartime waiver (abandoned: EC007-11, EC010-9); a memorandum adds a concept only where it does something none of these does, and says so; EC005-8 and EC005-9 are stale since memorandum 013 and are not cited as live (the user's request of 25 Nov 2026 to find redundant, stale and combinable operations and use cases; R05)
- **DIRR05-2** · A memorandum or review that adds to a battle or operation already in the chapters replaces its figure rather than adding an increment: it gives the new total once, with each provision's part named beside it, and checks its cases against the earlier memoranda's before it claims a share (R05: Dong Xoai had carried five successive figures for the allied dead and the Ia Drang four)
- **DIRR05-3** · Prose that takes a narrative approach tells the scene that proves the point: a person, a place, a moment and what happened, so that the reader sees the claim happen; a comparison of weapons, figures or capabilities that a sentence only asserts ("the M2 carbine was outgunned by the AK-47") goes into a table or a plain statement instead, and a paragraph is never a list of facts dressed as narrative (the user's ruling of 25 Nov 2026, extending DIRCP04-4 beyond the experience-of-the-war passages to all narrative prose)
- **DIRR06-1** · A study teaches its subject before it tells the war: after its Summary, a Primer sets out what the area is, as a reader new to it would need, covering every weapon, aircraft, vessel, unit or programme in it, what each is and how it was used, including what this war left unchanged; and an Inventory counts every category of item in the area by branch and by force, with exact quantities, a description and its use, the record's own figures where they exist and sourced historical figures otherwise, estimates marked as such; comparisons go in tables and narrative passages are scenes from one person's point of view (DIRR05-3) (the user's rulings of 25 Nov 2026; R06)
- **DIRR07-1** · The exercise's own estimates are presented as narrow ranges around the best estimate (RULES A12b: about a fifth of the midpoint; a share about 5 points; a difference about a third of its larger end), and the real uncertainty is carried by the confidence label, never dropped, with one plain clause where it is much wider than the range shown; history's figures and measured indicators are given as their sources give them (the user's ruling of 25 Nov 2026; R07)

## Gap register (latest status)

- **G-1** · A state without a foundation · narrowed · Land, police, merit chiefs and the Commission give the Republic a government in the held belt from 1964; it is captured by the palace when the American lever lapses in 1970–71, and its foundation in the countryside does not carry into the conventional war (CP01)
- **G-2** · Who holds the countryside after dark · narrowed · III and IV Corps hold about 8–14 and 6–12 points more of their rural people after dark than history's by 1967 and about 3–9 points more at the end of 1974 (POSCP03-3); from 1964 a gunship answers a post inside the net within 15–30 minutes on a clear night, and from 1969 the VNAF's radar gunships answer about two-thirds of the posts through cloud (POS015-1, POS015-3); the Front moved to the cloud, the hamlet's edge and the posts beyond the net, and I and II Corps never moved more than a few points
- **G-3** · Identifying the infrastructure inside the population · narrowed · The national file holds the enemy's political organisation to the end of 1975 and warns of where, not when (POSCP03-2); the raid force drove the senior apparatus it names across the Cambodian border by 1967, so the file names men nobody can reach (POS014-1)
- **G-4** · The officer corps: selection, leadership, desertion, corruption · narrowed · Below the regiment the RVNAF is led by board-chosen, educated officers and schooled NCOs from 1965–66, two-fifths to a half fewer battalions are broken in 1966–67, and the enemy declines them; the divisions and corps stay the palace's choices, and the decisive commands of 1972 and 1975 are chosen as historically (CP02)
- **G-5** · The American political clock · open · The provisions saved about 4,100–9,500 American lives on the record's rates (POSCP04-1), about 7–16 percent of the war's dead; tolerance is unmoved in every phase, and the fiscal 1975 appropriation is larger than history's only because there was no Watergate (POS011-1)
- **G-6** · Advisory leverage and its limits · open · The Aid Compliance Board is a real lever until 1969 and lapses with the withdrawal; it was used for governance and never for the RVNAF's self-sufficiency (CP01)
- **G-7** · Finding and fixing the main force · open · The enemy is easier to see in the open and exactly as hard to find under canopy; he still chooses every fight except the siege (CP01)
- **G-8** · Sanctuary and the theory of attrition · open · Cambodia is counted from 1965 and its caches fall in ten days in 1970; from 1967 it also holds the Front's provincial government of the upper Delta and the Saigon belt, driven there by the raids (C014-2), and the sanctuaries still regenerate the main force in every phase
- **G-9** · The Trail: throughput required against capacity · open · The opening strike on the North gave the Trail a second cause of its larger capacity: the trucks Moscow sent in place of heavy plant (C013-1); bombing still taxes arrivals by about a tenth at best, and the South's needs are a few tens of tons a day (POSTNA-4)
- **G-10** · The measurement problem · narrowed · R03 put every variable in a natural unit and entered 45 of history's figures; about 60 headline anchors remain unresearched, among them refugees, legitimacy, VCI strength and enemy initiative at the end of 1971, which CP04 judged as differences from history without history's figure, and the ledger of the Republic's small arms after 1966 (small-arms study Q-4)
- **G-11** · The sea and Sihanoukville · narrowed · The sea route closed in 1964; Sihanoukville opened eighteen months early and was counted, not stopped, until Lon Nol closed it in 1970 (CP01)
- **G-12** · Air power against a dispersed, night-moving enemy · narrowed · Decisive against the fixed and the measured, nothing against a society that has stopped owning anything worth a guided bomb (POSCP03-1); at night over a post the gunships of memorandum 015 hold the clear nights, and the Vietnamese radar gunships the cloudy ones, but no gunship flies over a PAVN division with its own air defence (POS015-4)
- **G-13** · No single manager of the war · open · CORDS on its historical date and form; the provisions created no single manager, only better inheritances for it (CP01)
- **G-14** · No lever on Hanoi's will · open · The heaviest opening blow the record holds moved Hanoi's will not at all (rung 4 throughout, R03) and its timing only through a Republic that did not collapse (EVMT01-4)
- **G-15** · The theater base · open · Unchanged by any provision; the rearmament's ammunition and the J's kits ride the historical base (CP01)
- **G-16** · Personnel spaces · narrowed · Unit rotation, a selected eighteen-month advisory corps, drill sergeants and NCO schools draw on one pool of American senior NCOs, bringing the 1967 shortage forward three to six months and deepening it; spaces remain trivial against a ceiling of none, and nothing a provision has built survives the withdrawal of 1973 (CP02)
- **G-17** · The soldier's family · open · The devaluation of June 1966 cut the private's rice by a third and his trained desertion carried the course to the Front around Saigon; no provision has touched pay against inflation, dependants' housing or the movement of families, and in March 1975 the corps dissolved toward them (CP02)
- **G-18** · Civilian harm has no holder · open · POP.civilian_harm is pushed by more than a dozen provisions and judged nowhere outside one study value; from 1964 the merit list's district chiefs clear fire within 300 metres of a post and become the arbiters of harm beside the hamlets at night (C015-1), and from 1970 those chiefs are the palace's choices; the record does not say whether harm rose after 1970, and a study or checkpoint must judge it by phase (air-war study Q-6)
- **G-19** · The war in northern Laos and on the rivers · open · The record holds no account of Barrel Roll and the Plain of Jars after 1964, nor of the riverine and coastal war after 1965 (Game Warden, the Vietnamese Navy's river groups, Market Time's later years); each shapes the Trail, the Delta and the sea route the provisions touched (air-war Q-4, maritime Q-3, Q-4)

### Phase I — The advisory war and escalation (Jan 1964 – Jul 1965)

*End of phase against the historical state: POP.night_control +2 to +6 against history (low) · POP.night_control.I_corps 0 to +3 against history (low) · POP.night_control.II_corps 0 to +3 against history (low) · POP.night_control.III_corps +3 to +8 against history (low) · POP.night_control.IV_corps +3 to +9 against history (low) · GVN.political_stability 3–5 (history 4; low) · VCI.strength -20% to -10% against history (medium) · TRAIL.tonnage_arriving -5% to +5% against history (low) · FIND.vci +0.3 to +1 against history (medium) · ARVN.effectiveness.small_unit +1 to +5 against history (low) · ARVN.self_sufficiency.fire_support 0 to +2 against history (low) · US.casualties 1,250–1,335 (history 1,369; low).*

The war that COMUSMACV inherits on 1 January 1964 is an advisory war that is being lost. The coup of 1 November 1963 had killed Ngo Dinh Diem and his brother Nhu, and with them went the province chiefs, the Strategic Hamlet Program and most of the Republic's administrative continuity. MACV under General Paul D. Harkins is a headquarters of advisers, helicopter companies and support troops; about 23,300 Americans are in the country by the end of 1964, none in combat units, and 147 die by hostile action that year [H40]. The fighting is done by the ARVN, the Regional and Popular Forces and the CIDG camps against a Viet Cong movement rebuilt since 1959 on the Viet Minh's old infrastructure and on cadres returning down the Trail.

The phase is a double collapse and a double response. In Saigon the state comes apart, coup after coup, and the generals spend more of their energy on each other than on the countryside. In the field the Viet Cong form regiments and then a division around Saigon, and at Binh Gia, Ba Gia and Dong Xoai they beat the general reserve on ground they chose. Hanoi commits regular PAVN regiments to the South for the first time. Washington answers from the air, first with reprisals and then, from 2 March 1965, with an opening strike on the North's whole target list and a campaign run from Saigon without zones or pauses (EV013-1); and on the ground, from two Marine battalions guarding an airfield in March to the decision of July to fight the war with American troops. Every constraint that will shape the war is drawn here except the one this war never drew, the restricted zones around Hanoi and Haiphong (P013b), and so is the enemy's basic answer to American firepower: close in, choose the time of battle, keep the base areas beyond the border.

Most of what is new in this war stood on its first day, and none of it decided the coups or the summer offensive. The Republic itself was changed by one session of decrees on 1 January 1964: land to the tiller and a Commission Against Corruption with an American power to suspend aid behind it, a resident rural police with a Special Branch, province and district chiefs chosen from a ranked list, Phung Hoang centres built on the police's files, an officer board and a combined command (EVR05-1). Behind those decrees stood what had been built since 1957 and was already in the ranks: every private and territorial trained on the 2026 course, every NCO schooled for his grade, every officer educated before each promotion, and an industry a generation above the country's own (EVR05-1) [M007] [M009]. By July 1965 about 330,000 hectares are titled, the musters have found the RVNAF about 41,000 men smaller than its rolls (EVR05-2) [X-001], and about 1,100 village posts stand in the held belt, where a post with its trained and rearmed Popular Forces platoon now holds about nineteen attacks in twenty (EV002-2) [X-009]. The Front's answer is to move its committees out of the held villages, and the first campaigns of the task force, of Delta and of the district centres follow them out (EVR05-3).

The command can also see and strike as history's could not. The Global Hawk orbit closes the trawler route within a year and moves Hanoi's southern supply to Sihanoukville about eighteen months early (EV003-1); on the night of 4 August 1964 the radar shows no torpedo boats, and Pierce Arrow is not flown (EV000-3). Sixty-four AC-130J gunships fly over the posts from the first week, and by the summer of 1965 the Front has stopped assaulting the posts within their net on clear nights (EV015-1). The B-52Js wait on Guam for sixteen months with a target list and no authority, and then destroy in a week what history's fighter-bombers spent years on (EV013-1). The North disperses, Moscow and Beijing rebuild its sky (EVCP02-2), and nothing that reaches the South changes: the porters, the trucks and the Front's regiments notice nothing at all (F013-7).
